brief.headline: Defense stocks are moving in two directions: the big contractors and government tech firms are climbing, while space, drone and aircraft parts stocks keep sliding.
summary: The defense ETF slipped 1.1% on Friday and is down about 5% over the past month, while the S&P 500 is close to flat. That average hides a wide gap. Lockheed Martin is up 15% in a month after beating earnings estimates, Palantir, CACI and Science Applications all sit within 8% of their 52-week highs, and Leidos has climbed 10% this month on a new Pentagon AI contract.

The losses are concentrated in smaller, faster-growing names and in aircraft parts. Drone stocks are down about 26% on average this month and space stocks about 23%, with Rocket Lab pushing its larger Neutron rocket into next year. Metal and parts suppliers fell hard last week too: Carpenter Technology dropped 24.5%, Howmet 16% and ATI 15.5% in five days.
watch: Boeing reports on Tuesday, Oct. 27, its first results since the 737 MAX 10 was cleared to carry passengers.
A heavy run of earnings on Thursday, Oct. 29: L3Harris, Huntington Ingalls, Howmet, Textron, Leonardo DRS and ATI, with General Dynamics on Friday.
Palantir reports on Nov. 2, the day before the midterm elections, which could change how investors think about future defense budgets.

GE.take: GE Aerospace fell 9% last week and is down 21% over three months, even though analysts still rate it a strong buy. The drop followed its Oct. 20 earnings report and lined up with a broad selloff in jet engine and parts suppliers like Howmet and Carpenter.
good: Wall Street's average rating is still Strong Buy
The largest company in the defense ETF, about 19% of the fund
risks: Heavy selling last week, at about 1.7 times normal volume
27% below its 52-week high with no clear turn yet
GE.watch: Whether selling in aircraft parts makers eases after Howmet and ATI report on Oct. 29.

RTX.take: RTX beat earnings expectations on Oct. 20 and added new Pentagon contracts last week, but the stock has gone mostly sideways for a month. It is up 4% this year while the defense ETF is down about 6%.
good: Latest quarter came in better than expected
New contract awards added to an already large order backlog
risks: Still 16% below its high after a three-month slide
Some analysts think the price already reflects the good news
RTX.watch: More Pentagon contract announcements and any defense budget news around the Nov. 3 midterms.

BA.take: Boeing is down 13% this year and drifting lower ahead of its earnings report on Tuesday. The 737 MAX 10 was just cleared to carry passengers, though one 777 freighter production line has been idle for two months.
good: The MAX 10 approval ends a long-running delay
risks: Its finance chief has already said cash flow is less likely to beat targets

LMT.take: Lockheed Martin jumped 9% last week after beating earnings estimates and landing an F-35 deal, and it is now up 25% this year. It is one of the best performers in the group over the past month.
good: Earnings beat plus new contract wins
Up 25% this year while the defense ETF is down
risks: The climb has been very fast, and pullbacks are common after runs like this
LMT.watch: Whether it holds last week's gains as other contractors report this week.

NOC.take: Northrop Grumman rose 6% last week after its Oct. 20 report, where it kept its full-year forecast unchanged. The stock is up 8% this month but still 29% below its 52-week high.
good: Stuck to its 2026 outlook, which investors took well
The trend has turned up over the past month
risks: Still well below last year's high
Getting a little stretched after a quick climb
NOC.watch: Pentagon contract news and defense budget talk around the midterm elections.

GD.take: General Dynamics has recovered 4% this month after a weak summer, helped by a new Navy electronic attack contract. It also named a new head for its government IT business, GDIT.
good: Holding up better than the defense ETF this year
risks: Traders expect roughly a 3.5% move either way on earnings

LHX.take: L3Harris is up 7% this month on new Navy jamming and Pentagon contracts, but it is still down 13% this year and a third below its high. It reports earnings Thursday.
good: New contract wins, including a Navy jammer deal
risks: Earnings on Oct. 29 are the next big test

HII.take: Huntington Ingalls, the Navy's main shipbuilder, is down 19% this year and 40% from its high. It added contract work and raised its dividend recently, but the stock has not found much footing.
good: New work tied to the US, UK and Australia submarine program
risks: UK shipbuilder Babcock is pushing to build warships for the US Navy, a possible new competitor

HWM.take: Howmet Aerospace, which makes jet engine parts, fell 16% last week over five straight down days and hit a new 52-week low. Headlines point to fallout from a plant incident, and RBC cut its price target to $300.
good: Analysts still rate it Strong Buy on average
risks: Heavy selling, at 1.7 times normal volume
HWM.watch: Earnings on Thursday, Oct. 29, which should say more about the plant issue.

TDG.take: TransDigm fell 3.2% on Friday after Morgan Stanley cut its price target to $1,300, and it is down 17% this year. Like other aircraft parts makers, it has been caught in the group's recent selloff.
good: Flat over the past month while many parts peers fell harder
risks: Trading below both its 50-day and 200-day average prices
TDG.watch: How other parts makers' earnings go this week, since the group has been moving together.

TXT.take: Textron, maker of Cessna jets and Bell helicopters, has been flat for a month after a 20% slide over the summer. It plans to separate part of its industrial business and just built its first Citation CJ4 Gen3 jet.
good: New Cessna orders and a new jet in production
The planned separation could make the company simpler
risks: Investors will want an update on the split at earnings

AXON.take: Axon, maker of Tasers and police body cameras, bounced 8% last week after a steep selloff and launched its new Body 5 camera. The stock is still down 26% this year and 45% from its high.
good: Raymond James still has a much higher price target
risks: Last week's bounce is small next to this year's losses

PLTR.take: Palantir is up about 50% over three months and sits 8% below its high, making it the strongest large company in the group. It reports earnings on Monday, Nov. 2, and expectations are high after that run.
good: Tied for the highest score on the page
Steady gains on normal trading volume
risks: A 50% three-month gain means a lot is expected from the Nov. 2 report

CACI.take: CACI is up 28% over three months and close to its high after an earnings report where profit margins improved and contract wins were strong, even though revenue came in a little light. Analysts were split afterward, with Stifel raising its target and UBS lowering its own.
good: Better profit margins and strong contract wins
One of the highest scores on the page
risks: Some analysts think the stock got expensive after the rally
CACI.watch: New government IT and defense tech contract awards.

LDOS.take: Leidos climbed 14% during an eight-day winning streak after landing a Pentagon AI contract. It is up 18% over three months but still down 25% this year.
good: New AI and cyber contracts with the Pentagon
Price is back above its 50-day average
risks: Has climbed fast in a short time
Still a third below its 52-week high

SAIC.take: Science Applications is up 45% this year and trading right at its 52-week high after a 10% gain this month. It recently reshuffled its finance leadership.
good: Steady climb to a new high
Up 45% this year while the defense ETF is down
risks: Wall Street's average rating is only Hold
Running hot after a quick climb
SAIC.watch: Its next earnings report and new government tech contracts.

BAH.take: Booz Allen reported on Oct. 23: profit beat expectations and it raised its profit forecast, but sales slipped as civilian government work declined. The stock is up 6% this month but still 28% below its high.
good: Better margins in the latest quarter
risks: Revenue fell, mostly from civilian agency work
Wall Street's average rating is Hold
BAH.watch: Whether the civilian contract slowdown spreads or levels off next quarter.

PSN.take: Parsons has bounced 16% this month but is still down 42% over the past year. It just won federal approval for a soil cleanup technology aimed at so-called forever chemicals, and it reports earnings Wednesday.
good: Federal approval for its PFAS cleanup technology
Strong bounce over the past month
risks: Earnings will show whether the recovery holds

VVX.take: V2X is up 36% this year but cooled off over the summer, down 15% in three months. It recently showed new counter-drone and AI systems at the Army's big annual trade show.
good: Still well ahead for the year
risks: Thin trading this week, about half the usual volume

BBAI.take: BigBear.ai is down 60% this year and 24% in the past month, even after announcing $225 million in contract wins. It reports earnings Tuesday, and analysts expect a loss.

RKLB.take: Rocket Lab is down 29% this month and 65% from its high after pushing the first launch of its larger Neutron rocket into next year. A partner of AST SpaceMobile is also challenging Rocket Lab's planned purchase of Iridium.
good: Analysts still rate it Buy on average
risks: The Neutron delay pushes back a key source of future revenue
The Iridium deal faces a regulatory challenge
RKLB.watch: Earnings on Monday, Nov. 9, and any new Neutron timeline.

LUNR.take: Intuitive Machines is down 33% in a month and 78% from its high, sliding with the rest of the small space stocks. It added Dr. Christopher Scolese to its board last week.
good: Analysts' average rating is Strong Buy
risks: Trading has been quiet, with no sign of buyers returning yet
LUNR.watch: News on upcoming NASA moon missions.

FLY.take: Firefly Aerospace rose 9% last week after progress on a NASA lunar mission and a design milestone for its Elytra spacecraft. It is still down 21% this month and 71% below its high.
good: Elytra spacecraft passed a key design review
risks: A newer, smaller public company that can swing hard either way

VOYG.take: Voyager Technologies jumped 5% on Friday but is down 19% over the past month. Investors are watching its Starlab commercial space station project.
good: Starlab could become a new way to invest in commercial space
risks: Trading has been lighter than usual

KRMN.take: Karman signed a $218 million deal with Lockheed Martin to support THAAD missile interceptor production, and the stock rose 6% on Friday. Even so, it is down half this year and Piper Sandler cut its target from $91 to $59.
good: Up 5% this month while most space stocks fell

RDW.take: Redwire won a $21.5 million Air Force drone contract and a new Axiom Space station job last week, but the stock is still down 28% this month. It remains up 10% for the year.
good: Two new contracts in one week
risks: Recent contract wins have not stopped the slide
RDW.watch: Whether more contract news can turn the trend.

PL.take: Planet Labs launched its 12th Pelican imaging satellite last week, but the stock is down 36% over three months. It has fallen along with other small space companies.
good: Satellite fleet keeps growing with each launch
Analysts rate it Buy on average
PL.watch: Upcoming satellite launches and new government imaging contracts.

BKSY.take: BlackSky's CEO and CFO both sold shares last week under pre-set trading plans, and the stock is down 24% this month. It bounced 5% on Friday.
good: The insider sales were under pre-set plans, which are routine

SPIR.take: Spire Global is down 26% this month but still up 21% for the year. An analyst upgraded it to Buy in mid-October with a $15 price target.
risks: Very small company, worth around $400 million
SPIR.watch: Whether the recent upgrade brings buyers back.

ASTS.take: AST SpaceMobile is down 35% this month and 45% this year. Scotiabank upgraded it last week, and Roth says SpaceX's push into cell service could help the wider industry.
good: Rose on Thursday even as the market fell
risks: Faces direct competition from SpaceX in phone-to-satellite service
ASTS.watch: The dispute over Rocket Lab's Iridium deal and its next satellite launches.

KTOS.take: Kratos hit a new 52-week low last week and is down 49% this year. Oppenheimer started covering it with a positive rating and a $50 target, pointing to its large order backlog.
good: Analysts rate it Strong Buy on average
KTOS.watch: Pentagon drone program news and its next earnings report.

AVAV.take: AeroVironment, maker of military drones, is down 49% this year and hit a 52-week low last week before bouncing 5% on Friday. Cathie Wood's ARK fund has been buying shares.
good: ARK Invest has been adding shares
risks: One of the worst performers in the market this year

RCAT.take: Red Cat is down 35% this month. Its plan to buy Steyr Motors raised concerns that it will issue more shares, though it also launched a line of crewless boats the Navy can now order.
good: New uncrewed boat line available to the Navy
risks: The Steyr deal may mean issuing more shares
Lowest score in the drone group
RCAT.watch: Details on how the Steyr purchase will be paid for.

ONDS.take: Ondas is down 18% this month and 37% this year, despite launching an AI product with Palantir. Retail traders remain enthusiastic, but the stock keeps drifting lower.
risks: Light trading, about half the usual volume

UMAC.take: Unusual Machines landed a $16.9 million order and is buying a drone battery maker for $52 million. Northland started coverage with a positive rating, but the stock is still down 29% this month.
risks: The acquisition adds cost and risk

AIRO.take: AIRO Group fell another 10% last week and is down 34% this month after analysts lowered their earnings expectations. It did qualify to compete for Canadian military drone work through 2031.
good: Eligible for Canada's military drone program

DRS.take: Leonardo DRS won a $500 million counter-drone contract and a NASA deal, but the stock is down 29% over three months. It reports earnings Thursday.
risks: Selling has picked up, at 1.3 times normal volume

MRCY.take: Mercury Systems is down 28% over three months. Oppenheimer started covering it last week with a positive rating.
good: New analyst coverage with a positive rating
Still slightly up for the year
risks: A director plans to sell some shares

CW.take: Curtiss-Wright hit a new 52-week low last week and is down 38% over three months. Morgan Stanley cut its price target from $860 to $625, even as the company keeps winning nuclear power work like a TerraPower simulator.
risks: Steep three-month slide with heavy selling

OSIS.take: OSI Systems, which makes security scanners, has held steady for a month after a weak first half of the year. New contracts are drawing attention ahead of its earnings report Thursday.

MOG-A.take: Moog is up 40% this year but slipped 7% last week as aircraft parts stocks sold off. It was also shuffled between Russell index funds last week, which can cause short-term swings.
risks: Some analysts think the price already reflects the good results
MOG-A.watch: Whether the aircraft parts selloff spreads further.

ATRO.take: Astronics, which makes aircraft lighting and power systems, is down 16% this month though still up 34% for the year. KeyBanc started covering it with a neutral rating.
good: Still well up for the year
Posted a record quarter in its last report
ATRO.watch: How other aircraft parts makers' results land this week.

BWXT.take: BWX Technologies, which builds nuclear reactors for Navy ships, is down 26% this year. It slid after saying no decision has been made on a nuclear project in Poland, despite a strong order backlog.

ACHR.take: Archer Aviation is down 48% this year and 32% this month. It announced plans for air taxi service in Texas, but the stock keeps sliding.
good: Analysts rate it Buy on average
risks: Still early, with little revenue so far

JOBY.take: Joby Aviation is down 64% this year and has the lowest score on the page. Certification delays have weighed on it, though it recently tested a hydrogen-powered aircraft.

BETA.take: Beta Technologies rose 10% last week after the FAA cleared it for electric aircraft demonstration flights. Its CEO sold about $560,000 in stock around the same time.
good: Up 10% over three months, unlike other air taxi stocks

FTAI.take: FTAI Aviation, which leases and repairs jet engines, hit a 52-week low last week and is 52% below its high. Questions about profit margins and its push into power generation have weighed on it.

WWD.take: Woodward, which makes aircraft and engine control systems, fell 8% last week with other aircraft parts stocks and is down 28% over three months. It is roughly flat for the year.
good: Recent analyst notes praise how well it runs
risks: Some analysts think the stock is still expensive
WWD.watch: Whether the aircraft parts selloff eases.

ATI.take: ATI, a maker of specialty metals for jet engines, fell 15.5% last week as aerospace metal stocks sold off, led by Carpenter Technology's 24.5% drop. It is still up 37% this year.
good: Analysts expect earnings growth when it reports
risks: Below its 50-day average after a fast drop

CRS.take: Carpenter Technology plunged 24.5% last week after its earnings and new guidance disappointed investors, and it has lost half its value in three months. A law firm has announced an investigation on behalf of shareholders.
good: Analysts still rate it Strong Buy on average
risks: Very heavy selling, 1.75 times normal volume
Shareholder legal investigation and price target cuts
CRS.watch: Whether ATI reports similar trouble on Oct. 29.

HEI.take: HEICO has held up better than most aircraft parts makers this month, down only 3%, though it is off 17% over three months. Analysts have been raising their earnings estimates.
risks: Morgan Stanley trimmed its price target to $345
HEI.watch: How peers' results land this week.

HXL.take: Hexcel, which makes lightweight composite materials for aircraft, fell 12% last week after its earnings showed softer defense sales and pressure on profit margins. RBC and Morgan Stanley both cut their price targets.
good: Commercial aerospace sales are still growing
risks: Very heavy selling, 2.4 times normal volume

SARO.take: StandardAero, an engine repair company, has steadied this month after a 26% three-month slide. Investors are worried about engine repair demand in 2027.

LOAR.take: Loar Holdings dropped 5% on Friday and is down 14% over three months. Morgan Stanley lowered its target to $72, and some analysts point to its high debt.

DCO.take: Ducommun is up 65% this year, one of the best runs in the group, but has pulled back 10% this month. Guggenheim started coverage with a Buy rating and a $246 target in early October.
risks: Pulling back with other parts makers

VSEC.take: VSE fell 13% last week and is down 21% this month, even though it posted record results and raised guidance earlier in October. It has been caught in the wider aviation parts selloff.

AIR.take: AAR is down 21% this month after announcing a large acquisition, though it is still up 15% for the year. A board member sold about $425,000 in stock last week.
good: Beat earnings estimates in its last report
AIR.watch: Updates on how the acquisition is going.

CDRE.take: Cadre Holdings, which makes body armor and safety gear, jumped 14% last week, recovering from a 52-week low earlier this month. It pays a quarterly dividend and reports earnings Nov. 4.
risks: Its strategy leans heavily on buying other companies

NPK.take: National Presto, best known for kitchen appliances but also a large ammunition maker, is up 40% this year and near its high. It has a $1.81 billion defense order backlog, though some analysts think the stock has run ahead of earnings.
risks: Some analysts say earnings need to catch up with the price
Small company with no Wall Street rating listed

RGR.take: Sturm Ruger is up 39% this year. Italian gunmaker Beretta completed an offer to buy 2.4 million Ruger shares, with more holders trying to sell than it accepted, and the stock fell 4.4% on Friday as the offer closed.
good: Tied for the highest score on the page
Beretta now owns a bigger stake

SWBI.take: Smith & Wesson agreed to buy Savage Arms for $160 million in stock and cash. Shares fell 4.5% on Friday but are still up 39% this year.
risks: Deal is paid partly in new shares
SWBI.watch: Updates on closing the Savage Arms deal.
